project.name: wing
project.description: Hermes Wing — an independent cross-platform Flutter client for Hermes Agent sessions, streamed runs, approvals, profiles, and device speech.

nodes.name: flutter_semantics.mjs
nodes.summary: Shared Playwright helper module for driving the Flutter web build through its accessibility (flt-semantics) DOM: enables the semantics tree, activates hidden nodes, and dispatches click/long-press events on labeled elements. Also exports the APP_URL and semantic selector constants used by every browser spec.
nodes.languageNotes: Flutter web renders no normal DOM; interaction happens by dispatching synthetic events on flt-semantics elements matched via aria-label.

nodes.name: enableFlutterAccessibility
nodes.summary: Activates Flutter web's semantics tree by clicking the hidden accessibility placeholder, then waits for flt-semantics nodes to appear. Called by every browser spec before interacting with the app.

nodes.name: activateVisibleSemantics
nodes.summary: Dispatches staggered click events on all currently visible interactive flt-semantics elements to force Flutter to hydrate their semantic roles.

nodes.name: clickSemantic
nodes.summary: Finds the interactive semantic element whose aria-label contains the given text and dispatches pointerdown/pointerup/click events on it, returning whether a match was clicked.

nodes.name: longPressSemantic
nodes.summary: Simulates a long-press gesture on a labeled semantic button by dispatching pointerdown, waiting past the long-press threshold, then dispatching pointerup.

nodes.name: browser-surfaces.spec.mjs
nodes.summary: Playwright regression spec covering top-level browser surfaces of the Wing web app, opening routes directly and in a connected-gateway state via the wingE2EHermesConnect test hook.

nodes.name: chat-tts.spec.mjs
nodes.summary: Extensive Playwright regression spec for chat text-to-speech: installs a speechSynthesis recorder stub, drives voice settings (speak replies toggle, reply speed), sends chat messages through the composer with approval flow, and asserts spoken-reply behavior with screenshots.
nodes.languageNotes: Stubs the browser speechSynthesis API via page.addInitScript with a recorder that captures utterances, speak attempts, and cancellations for assertions.

nodes.name: installSpeechSynthesisRecorder
nodes.summary: Injects an init script replacing window.speechSynthesis with a recording fake that tracks utterances, speak attempts, and cancel calls, and simulates utterance start/end callbacks.

nodes.name: connectFromVoiceSettings
nodes.summary: Opens the voice settings surface, enables the speak-replies toggle, sets reply speed to 1.25x, then connects to the E2E Hermes session, capturing screenshots along the way.

nodes.name: hermes-lifecycle.spec.mjs
nodes.summary: Playwright regression spec for Hermes session lifecycle: connects to the E2E gateway via the wingE2EHermesConnect hook and verifies session-level UI such as the Sessions control using semantic labels.

nodes.name: openConnectedHermes
nodes.summary: Navigates to the app, waits for the wingE2EHermesConnect test hook, enables accessibility, connects to the E2E Hermes gateway, and asserts the Sessions button is visible.

nodes.name: hermes-live-api.spec.mjs
nodes.summary: Opt-in Playwright spec that exercises a real live Hermes gateway (via WING_LIVE_HERMES_URL environment variables) rather than the E2E stub, verifying basic API connectivity from the web client.

nodes.name: hermes-live-say-hi.spec.mjs
nodes.summary: Opt-in live Playwright spec that connects to a real Hermes gateway, sends a constrained greeting prompt, and asserts the agent replies with 'hi', proving an end-to-end chat round trip.

nodes.name: hermes-provider-chat.spec.mjs
nodes.summary: Playwright regression spec covering provider-backed chat in the web client, locating UI via flt-semantics aria-labels to drive and verify a provider chat exchange.

nodes.name: hermes-smoke.spec.mjs
nodes.summary: Smoke-level Playwright spec for the Wing web build, using semanticLabel/semanticText locator helpers over the flt-semantics tree to verify core surfaces load and key controls are present.

nodes.name: e2e-screenshots.spec.mjs
nodes.summary: Small Playwright spec that opens app routes with accessibility enabled purely to capture end-to-end screenshots of the web build.

nodes.name: desktop_host_commands.h
nodes.summary: Shared constants header defining Win32 menu command IDs (settings, about, minimize, maximize, full screen) and the desktop_host_commands MethodChannel name and method used to bridge native window commands into the Flutter app.
nodes.languageNotes: Header-only constexpr constants in a dedicated namespace, shared by the window and entry-point translation units.

nodes.name: flutter_window.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the Win32 host window for the Flutter view: creates the FlutterViewController, wires the desktop_host_commands MethodChannel, builds the native application menu, and handles window messages including full-screen toggling and menu commands.
nodes.languageNotes: Extends the stock Flutter Windows runner with a native menu bar, a host-command MethodChannel to Dart, and manual full-screen state management via SetWindowLongPtr/WINDOWPLACEMENT.

nodes.name: flutter_window.h
nodes.summary: Declares the FlutterWindow class, a Win32Window subclass that hosts the Flutter view and holds the FlutterViewController, host-command MethodChannel, application menu handle, and full-screen restore state.

nodes.name: main.cpp
nodes.summary: Windows application entry point (wWinMain) that attaches a console when debugging, initializes COM, forwards command-line arguments to the Dart entrypoint, creates the FlutterWindow with keyboard accelerators, and runs the Win32 message loop.

nodes.name: utils.cpp
nodes.summary: Runner utility implementations: console creation/attachment with stream redirection, command-line argument parsing, and UTF-16 to UTF-8 string conversion for the Windows host.

nodes.name: utils.h
nodes.summary: Declares the Windows runner utility functions for console attachment, command-line argument retrieval, and UTF-16 to UTF-8 conversion.

nodes.name: FlutterWindow
nodes.summary: Win32Window subclass hosting the Flutter view; owns the FlutterViewController, the desktop_host_commands MethodChannel, the native menu handle, and windowed-placement state for full-screen toggling.

nodes.name: OnCreate
nodes.summary: Creates the FlutterViewController, registers plugins, sets up the desktop_host_commands MethodChannel, attaches the Flutter view as child content, and shows the window on first frame.

nodes.name: OnDestroy
nodes.summary: Tears down the host-command channel and Flutter controller, detaches and destroys the native application menu, then defers to the base window destroy handler.

nodes.name: CreateApplicationMenu
nodes.summary: Builds the native Win32 menu bar (App, Window, Help popups) with settings, minimize, maximize, full-screen, and about commands, with careful cleanup of partially built menus on failure.
nodes.languageNotes: Manual HMENU ownership: every AppendMenuW failure path explicitly DestroyMenu's the not-yet-adopted popups to avoid leaks.

nodes.name: ToggleFullScreen
nodes.summary: Toggles borderless full-screen by saving/restoring window style and placement, resizing to the current monitor bounds via MonitorFromWindow and SetWindowPos.

nodes.name: MessageHandler
nodes.summary: Handles WM_COMMAND menu/accelerator commands (open settings, about box, minimize, maximize, full screen), forwards unhandled messages to the Flutter engine, and reloads system fonts on WM_FONTCHANGE.

nodes.name: wWinMain
nodes.summary: Application entry point: attaches or creates a console, initializes COM, passes CLI args to the Dart project, creates the FlutterWindow with menu-command accelerators, and pumps the Win32 message loop until quit.

nodes.name: CreateAndAttachConsole
nodes.summary: Allocates a Win32 console, redirects stdout/stderr to it, and resyncs Flutter's output streams so engine logging is visible.

nodes.name: GetCommandLineArguments
nodes.summary: Parses the process command line via CommandLineToArgvW and returns the arguments (minus the executable name) converted to UTF-8 strings.

nodes.name: Utf8FromUtf16
nodes.summary: Converts a UTF-16 wide string to a UTF-8 std::string using WideCharToMultiByte with length and overflow checks.

nodes.name: MainActivity.kt
nodes.summary: Android host activity for the Flutter app that wires up the native platform channels: pairing-handoff connect payloads (with an EventChannel for new intents), ML Kit QR code scanning, device speech diagnostics, and the durable keystore channel.
nodes.languageNotes: Registers multiple MethodChannels plus one EventChannel in configureFlutterEngine, bridging Flutter to Android intents, ML Kit barcode scanning, and speech recognition service queries.

nodes.name: MainActivity
nodes.summary: FlutterActivity subclass that handles launch and follow-up connect intents, exposes QR scanning and speech diagnostics over MethodChannels, and registers the durable keystore channel.

nodes.name: onCreate
nodes.summary: Captures the connect payload from the launch intent before delegating to the FlutterActivity lifecycle.

nodes.name: configureFlutterEngine
nodes.summary: Registers all native channels with the Flutter engine: pairing connect payload and QR scan methods, device speech diagnostics, the DurableKeyStoreChannel handler, and an EventChannel streaming connect intents.

nodes.name: onNewIntent
nodes.summary: Parses connect payloads from intents delivered while the activity is running and emits them on the connect-intent event sink.

nodes.name: scanQrCode
nodes.summary: Runs a single ML Kit GmsBarcodeScanning QR scan with auto-zoom, guarding against concurrent scans and reporting success, cancellation, or failure back to the Flutter caller.

nodes.name: deviceSpeechDiagnostics
nodes.summary: Builds a DeviceSpeechDiagnostics snapshot from installed speech recognition services and microphone permission state, serialized for the MethodChannel.

nodes.name: querySpeechRecognitionServices
nodes.summary: Queries PackageManager for services handling the RecognitionService intent, using the API-level-appropriate queryIntentServices overload.

nodes.name: DeviceSpeechDiagnostics.kt
nodes.summary: Small data holder describing on-device speech recognition availability (recognition services and microphone permission) with a serializer for MethodChannel transport.

nodes.name: DeviceSpeechDiagnostics
nodes.summary: Carries the list of recognition service names and microphone permission flag, converting itself to a bounded map via toMethodChannelMap for Flutter consumption.

nodes.name: toMethodChannelMap
nodes.summary: Serializes the diagnostics into a map with a capped list of recognition services for safe MethodChannel transfer.

nodes.name: DurableKeyStoreChannel.kt
nodes.summary: MethodChannel handler exposing Android Keystore-backed ES256 (P-256) operations to Flutter: key pair creation, JOSE-format signing, key deletion, and public JWK export.
nodes.languageNotes: Keys live in the hardware-backed AndroidKeyStore; DER signatures are converted to JOSE format and public keys are exported as base64url P-256 JWK coordinates.

nodes.name: DurableKeyStoreChannel
nodes.summary: MethodCallHandler dispatching isAvailable, create, sign, and delete calls onto AndroidKeyStore ES256 primitives, with argument validation and structured error responses.

nodes.name: onMethodCall
nodes.summary: Routes incoming MethodChannel calls to the keystore operations, mapping invalid arguments and keystore failures to distinct error codes.

nodes.name: createEs256KeyPair
nodes.summary: Generates (or returns the existing) P-256 signing key pair under the given alias in AndroidKeyStore with SHA-256 digest and no user-auth requirement, returning the public JWK.

nodes.name: signEs256
nodes.summary: Signs a payload with the aliased keystore private key using SHA256withECDSA and converts the DER signature to JOSE format.

nodes.name: PairingHandoffIntentParser.kt
nodes.summary: Pure parser that turns incoming Android intents (wing:// connect deep links via ACTION_VIEW, or shared text via ACTION_SEND) into pairing handoff payloads for the Flutter side.
nodes.languageNotes: Kotlin object (singleton) with no Android framework dependencies, making the intent-parsing logic unit-testable off-device.

nodes.name: PairingHandoffIntentParser
nodes.summary: Singleton parser validating the wing scheme and connect host for direct app opens, and text mime types for shared text, producing PairingHandoffPayload results.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Entry point that dispatches on intent action: ACTION_VIEW routes to direct app-open URI parsing, ACTION_SEND to shared-text parsing, anything else yields null.

nodes.name: main.cc
nodes.summary: Linux desktop entry point that instantiates MyApplication and hands control to the GTK application run loop.

nodes.name: my_application.cc
nodes.summary: GTK application implementation for the Linux runner: builds the window with a native menu bar (Settings, About, Window, View), embeds the Flutter view, registers plugins, and opens a desktop_host_commands method channel so native menu actions (e.g. openSettings) reach the Dart side.
nodes.languageNotes: GObject-style C++ using G_DEFINE_TYPE with virtual method overrides (activate, local_command_line, startup, shutdown, dispose) and an FlMethodChannel bridge to Flutter.

nodes.name: my_application.h
nodes.summary: Public header declaring the MyApplication GObject type and the my_application_new() constructor used by the Linux runner entry point.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Process entry point: creates a MyApplication instance and runs it via g_application_run.

nodes.name: _MyApplication
nodes.summary: Instance struct for the MyApplication GObject, holding Dart entrypoint arguments and the desktop host-command method channel.

nodes.name: toggle_maximized_window_cb
nodes.summary: Menu callback that toggles the window between maximized and restored states.

nodes.name: toggle_fullscreen_window_cb
nodes.summary: Menu callback that checks the native GdkWindow fullscreen state and toggles fullscreen on the window (bound to F11).

nodes.name: create_application_menu
nodes.summary: Builds the native GTK menu bar (Hermes Wing, Window, View menus) with keyboard accelerators (Ctrl+comma for Settings, F11 for Full Screen) and wires each item to its callback.

nodes.name: my_application_activate
nodes.summary: Core activation handler: creates the application window (choosing header bar vs traditional title bar based on window manager), embeds the Flutter view with Dart entrypoint arguments, packs the menu bar above it, registers plugins, and sets up the host-command channel, deferring window show until the first Flutter frame.

nodes.name: my_application_local_command_line
nodes.summary: Captures command-line arguments as Dart entrypoint arguments, registers the application, and activates it locally.

nodes.name: resource.h
nodes.summary: Visual Studio resource header defining the IDI_APP_ICON identifier used by the Windows runner's .rc file to embed the application icon.

nodes.name: win32_window.h
nodes.summary: Declares the Win32Window base class that abstracts a high-DPI-aware native Windows window, providing lifecycle hooks (OnCreate/OnDestroy), message handling, and child-content hosting for the Flutter view.
nodes.languageNotes: Standard Flutter Windows runner template header; Point/Size structs and virtual hooks let FlutterWindow subclass it.

nodes.name: Win32Window
nodes.summary: Abstract base class wrapping an HWND with DPI-scaled creation, show/destroy lifecycle, quit-on-close behavior, and a SetChildContent slot where the Flutter view is parented.

nodes.name: win32_window.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the Win32Window class: registers the window class via a singleton registrar, creates a per-monitor-DPI-scaled window, dispatches Win32 messages (resize, focus, dark-mode changes), and applies the system dark/light theme through DWM.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a WindowClassRegistrar singleton with refcounted active-window tracking, and reads the registry AppsUseLightTheme value to toggle DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE.

nodes.name: WindowClassRegistrar
nodes.summary: Singleton that lazily registers the shared Win32 window class and unregisters it when the last window is destroyed.

nodes.name: EnableFullDpiSupportIfAvailable
nodes.summary: Dynamically loads User32's EnableNonClientDpiScaling to enable per-monitor DPI scaling of the non-client area on Windows versions that support it.

nodes.name: Create
nodes.summary: Creates the native window at a DPI-scaled origin and size using the registered window class, applies the current theme, and invokes the OnCreate hook.

nodes.name: Win32Window::WndProc
nodes.summary: Static window procedure that binds the Win32Window instance pointer into the HWND on WM_NCCREATE and forwards subsequent messages to the instance's MessageHandler.

nodes.name: MessageHandler
nodes.summary: Handles core window messages: destroy/quit, DPI change repositioning, resizing the hosted Flutter child view, focus forwarding, and theme change notifications.

nodes.name: Destroy
nodes.summary: Tears down the window, invoking OnDestroy, destroying the HWND, and unregistering the shared window class when no windows remain.

nodes.name: SetChildContent
nodes.summary: Parents the Flutter view's HWND into this window, sizes it to fill the client area, and gives it focus.

nodes.name: UpdateTheme
nodes.summary: Reads the AppsUseLightTheme registry value and applies immersive dark mode to the window title bar via DwmSetWindowAttribute.

nodes.name: provider-hermes-smoke

nodes.name: 0001-hermes-only-runtime.md
nodes.summary: ADR declaring Hermes Wing a Hermes-only companion limited to /hermes and /settings routes, dropping legacy Gormes gateway/profile/memory surfaces. Superseded by ADR 0011's cross-platform client scope.

nodes.name: 0002-riverpod-provider-seams.md
nodes.summary: ADR adopting Riverpod providers as the dependency-injection seam for app-level services, with tests and E2E entry points overriding providers instead of using global singletons.

nodes.name: 0003-go-router-hermes-settings-shell.md
nodes.summary: ADR choosing go_router with a single shell route and two destinations (/hermes and /settings), using prefix helpers for route matching. Superseded by ADR 0011's broader route scope.

nodes.name: 0004-hermes-endpoint-and-secret-storage.md
nodes.summary: ADR splitting persistence of Hermes endpoint metadata (shared preferences) from API keys (platform secure storage), with URL normalization that strips userinfo, query strings, and fragments before display or storage.

nodes.name: 0005-capability-gated-hermes-client.md
nodes.summary: ADR making the Hermes Agent capabilities document the source of truth for optional client behavior: surfaces degrade gracefully when endpoints are not advertised instead of assuming server support.

nodes.name: 0006-run-sse-approvals-and-stop-lifecycle.md
nodes.summary: ADR modeling Hermes runs as SSE-driven chat work: run events drive transcript deltas, tool progress, approvals, and stop controls, with per-session stream ownership, bounded timeouts, and durable detached-run leases for process-death recovery.

nodes.name: 0007-native-hermes-channel-not-wing-channel-adapter.md
nodes.summary: ADR keeping HermesChannel as the native public app seam (with HermesApiChannel as production implementation) instead of adapting Hermes behind the legacy Gormes-era WingChannel interface.

nodes.name: 0008-mobile-hermes-ui-with-telegram-ergonomics.md
nodes.summary: ADR using Hermes Desktop as the structural and status-language reference while adopting Telegram chat ergonomics on mobile (single-pane chat, bottom composer, sheets). Superseded by ADR 0011's full cross-platform scope.

nodes.name: 0009-local-device-voice-stt-tts.md
nodes.summary: ADR choosing local on-device voice: speech_to_text for capture (on-device only, fail closed), flutter_tts and the pinned pocket_speech package for speech output, with platform gating, lifecycle-driven capture cancellation, and no raw-speech logging.

nodes.name: 0010-validation-and-e2e-entrypoints.md
nodes.summary: ADR defining the layered validation ritual: flutter analyze, serialized flutter test, a web E2E build through lib/main_e2e.dart with JavaScript hooks, Playwright smoke tests, and platform builds in CI.

nodes.name: 0011-cross-platform-hermes-one-successor.md
nodes.summary: ADR redefining Hermes Wing as an independent cross-platform Hermes One client pursuing capability parity with Hermes Desktop, superseding the companion-only scope of ADRs 0001, 0003, and 0008.

nodes.name: 0012-hermes-agent-domain-authority.md
nodes.summary: ADR keeping Hermes Agent as the sole authority for domain state (profiles, config, memory, skills, sessions, gateway); Flutter clients use capability-advertised contracts and never reproduce Electron's direct config or database access.

nodes.name: 0013-adaptive-parity-route-tree.md
nodes.summary: ADR defining one adaptive route tree shared by mobile and desktop: Chat, Discover, Office, and Tasks as Android primaries plus administrative destinations behind More, with routes added only as working vertical slices.

nodes.name: 0014-single-origin-hermes-control-plane.md
nodes.summary: ADR requiring one canonical Hermes Agent API origin and bearer credential per endpoint profile, with /v1/capabilities as the source of truth; clients never reproduce Hermes Desktop's separate gateway/Dashboard transports.

nodes.name: 0015-scoped-remote-administration.md
nodes.summary: ADR requiring scoped operator tokens with domain-level read/write grants before exposing mutating remote administration; Hermes Agent enforces scopes on every route while client visibility is only a usability aid.

nodes.name: 0016-one-time-android-enrollment.md
nodes.summary: ADR defining Android enrollment via short-lived single-use pairing codes (QR or wing://connect), exchanged for a scoped token stored in secure storage; bearer credentials never appear in URLs, logs, or clipboard flows.

nodes.name: 0017-electron-retirement-after-desktop-parity.md
nodes.summary: ADR gating Electron (Hermes Desktop) retirement on the parity ledger: every baseline capability must be validated on Linux, Windows, and macOS before the gate opens; Android or single-platform success is not sufficient.

nodes.name: 0018-adaptive-office-renderers.md
nodes.summary: ADR adopting one platform-independent Office interaction model with adaptive renderers: Android ships an accessible 2D Office first while desktop targets must deliver the baseline 3D experience before Electron retirement.

nodes.name: 0019-separate-hermes-one-account-authority.md
nodes.summary: ADR keeping the optional Hermes One account service as a separate cloud identity authority: the app authenticates to it directly via OAuth rather than proxying through Hermes Agent, and account/wallet failures never break chat.

nodes.name: 0020-no-local-wallet-custody.md
nodes.summary: ADR refusing local wallet custody: Hermes Wing never stores or transfers wallet recovery phrases, shows only public wallet metadata, and treats legacy local wallets as migration data behind a guarded desktop export path.

nodes.name: 0021-freeze-final-electron-cutoff.md
nodes.summary: ADR freezing a final named Electron retirement cutoff: capability deltas between the Hermes Desktop 0.7.3 baseline and the cutoff must be validated, replaced, or deprecated in Hermes Wing, and Desktop accepts only critical fixes afterward.

nodes.name: 0022-additive-capability-schema.md
nodes.summary: ADR requiring parity APIs to evolve additively via a versioned /v1/capabilities document: clients ignore unknown fields, require advertised operations, and fail closed on unsupported schemas instead of keying off release versions.

nodes.name: 0023-external-managed-hermes-runtime.md
nodes.summary: ADR keeping the Hermes Agent runtime external to Hermes Wing packages: desktop host adapters discover or install an existing Hermes runtime and verify it via health and capability contracts, preserving independent release lifecycles.

nodes.name: 0024-profile-explicit-control-plane.md
nodes.summary: ADR making the Hermes control plane profile-explicit: one machine-scoped API service where every profile-owned operation carries validated profile identity and never depends on the mutable active_profile file or per-profile ports.

nodes.name: 0025-profile-query-context.md
nodes.summary: ADR mandating a `profile` query parameter on every profile-owned HTTP and SSE operation, failing closed on missing or malformed context and preserving the exact value across retries, pagination, and SSE reconnects.

nodes.name: 0026-http-and-sse-control-plane.md
nodes.summary: ADR choosing plain HTTP commands plus profile-scoped Server-Sent Events for asynchronous updates, with at-least-once delivery, resumable event IDs, GET reconciliation, and WebSocket reserved for genuinely bidirectional future use.

nodes.name: 0027-server-resource-handles.md
nodes.summary: ADR requiring attachments and context folders to cross the client-server boundary as opaque server-issued handles bound to profile and lifecycle policy, never as arbitrary client filesystem paths.

nodes.name: 0028-typed-revisioned-administration.md
nodes.summary: ADR defining remote administration as typed domain resources with atomic, revision-guarded mutations via If-Match (428/412 on missing or stale revisions) and presence-only secret fields, replacing generic get/set-config operations.

nodes.name: 0029-explicit-apply-lifecycle.md
nodes.summary: ADR making runtime application of admin changes explicit: mutations report an apply disposition (applied, reload_required, restart_required) and restarts occur only through a server-owned drain-and-apply operation with SSE progress.

nodes.name: 0030-no-offline-mutation-replay.md
nodes.summary: ADR forbidding durable offline queuing or automatic replay of mutations: disconnected read models are labeled stale, drafts stay inert until an explicit resend, and reconnection first refreshes authoritative server state.

nodes.name: 0031-explicit-electron-client-state-import.md
nodes.summary: ADR defining a previewable, explicit, one-time import of allowlisted non-secret Hermes Desktop client preferences on first launch, excluding credentials and domain state, with idempotent retries and value-free receipts.

nodes.name: 0032-accessible-capability-parity.md
nodes.summary: ADR making WCAG 2.2 AA plus platform accessibility conventions a capability-parity gate: semantics, keyboard operation, 200% text scaling, contrast, reduced motion, and an equivalent non-spatial presentation of the 3D Office.

nodes.name: 0033-signed-releases-and-updates.md
nodes.summary: ADR requiring platform release signing for every artifact and authenticated update metadata (version, channel, digest) for direct distribution, with fail-closed verification, staged channels, and confirmed non-interrupting updates.

nodes.name: 0034-explicit-minimal-analytics.md
nodes.summary: ADR keeping product analytics disabled by default with a closed event allowlist: opt-in creates a random install identifier, opt-out deletes it and drops pending events, and user content or identifiers are never eligible data.

nodes.name: 0035-baseline-locales-and-rtl.md
nodes.summary: ADR preserving the frozen 12-locale Hermes Desktop set with Flutter generated localization, locale-aware formatting, end-to-end RTL for Arabic and Hebrew, and CI plus per-locale layout evidence for critical flows.

nodes.name: 0036-server-owned-backup-and-restore.md
nodes.summary: ADR assigning backup and restore ownership to Hermes Agent via typed jobs and expiring archive handles: portable profile and passphrase-encrypted machine recovery modes, staged inspection with redacted previews, and all-or-rollback restore.

nodes.name: 0037-explicit-ssh-host-trust.md
nodes.summary: ADR requiring explicit fingerprint confirmation for SSH host trust in a Hermes Wing-owned known_hosts file with strict checking, hard-failing on changed keys, and an argument-vector-only execution boundary with loopback-bound tunnels.

nodes.name: 0038-verified-managed-runtime-installation.md
nodes.summary: ADR restricting Hermes Agent runtime install and update to signed, version-pinned release manifests with digest verification, unprivileged staged installs, OS-native elevation only, and verified side-by-side rollback on failure.

nodes.name: 0039-canonical-platform-packages.md
nodes.summary: ADR fixing a small canonical package matrix (AAB/APK, deb/RPM, MSIX, notarized DMG) with stable application identity across upgrades, no bundled Python or Hermes Agent, offline maintainer scripts, and data-preserving uninstall.

nodes.name: 0040-detach-android-background-runs.md
nodes.summary: ADR letting Android detach while server runs continue: backgrounding stops voice capture and invalidates client queues without stopping runs, resume reconciles authoritative state, and optional notifications carry no content or authorization.

nodes.name: 0041-picker-originated-filesystem-grants.md
nodes.summary: Accepted ADR requiring that Hermes filesystem access originate only from native picker selections registered with Hermes Agent, which returns opaque, expiring, principal-bound resource handles instead of raw paths. Specifies grant shape, path-traversal and symlink safety rules, and privacy/lifecycle guarantees that keep raw paths out of responses, logs, and diagnostics.

nodes.name: 0042-guarded-legacy-wallet-export.md
nodes.summary: Accepted ADR defining a guarded one-at-a-time legacy-wallet export in Hermes Desktop before Electron retirement, offering only a timed manual reveal or a passphrase-encrypted file behind user-presence verification. Enumerates prohibited flows (clipboard, QR, bulk, cloud) and the retirement evidence receipts that gate Electron shutdown.

nodes.name: 0043-hardened-hermes-one-device-authorization.md

Web is excluded until a separate Authorization Code + PKCE contract and token-storage review pass.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Hermes Wing is a cross-platform Flutter client that pairs once with a trusted Hermes Agent gateway and then runs live agent sessions from Android, web, or desktop. Start with the README for the session model and security boundaries, CONTEXT.md for the canonical product vocabulary (gateway, run, approval, transcript), and the ROADMAP for where the project is headed and what it deliberately will not do. These three documents define the terms every later step relies on.

tour.title: Application Bootstrap
tour.description: The production entry point is a one-line main() that runs WingApp, the root widget composing MaterialApp with Riverpod theme settings, localization, the router, and a desktop host command listener. pubspec.yaml is the manifest behind it all: Dart 3.12, Riverpod, go_router, secure storage, and the speech/TTS packages you will meet in later steps. Note how thin the entry point is — everything interesting is injected further down.
tour.languageLesson: Dart barrel files (like lib/app.dart) re-export symbols with a single 'export' directive, giving callers one stable import path while the implementation lives elsewhere.

tour.title: Adaptive Routing and Shell
tour.description: One go_router route tree serves both form factors: app_routes.dart holds the central path constants, and app_shell.dart wraps every routed screen in an adaptive navigation shell — bottom NavigationBar with an overflow sheet on mobile, NavigationRail with Hermes branding on desktop, switching on window width. ADR 0013 explains why a single adaptive tree was chosen over separate mobile and desktop apps, and docs/product/routes.md tables all eleven destinations.

tour.title: Wire JSON and Domain Models
tour.description: wing_json.dart is the project's shared wire-coercion library — tolerant string/int/bool readers and snake_case-vs-camelCase alias resolution — and it is one of the highest fan-in files in the codebase: nearly every domain model depends on it. On top of it sit the Hermes models: sessions with token and cost accounting, runs with a bounded lifecycle enum mapped from loose gateway status strings, and the capability document that gates what the client is allowed to show. Understanding this layer explains how the client survives gateway version drift.

tour.title: The Gateway HTTP Client
tour.description: The typed REST client covers health, capabilities, sessions, runs, SSE streaming, enrollment, profiles, providers, and models. hermes_api_config.dart owns endpoint parsing, auth headers, and URI builders for every route, while hermes_api_transport.dart abstracts the HTTP verbs so native (dart:io) and web platforms plug in different implementations. hermes_api.dart is the barrel that exports this whole surface to the rest of the app.
tour.languageLesson: Dart conditional imports ('if (dart.library.io) ...') select a platform implementation at compile time — the transport resolves to an io, web, or stub variant without any runtime checks.

tour.title: Streaming Runs and Approvals
tour.description: Live agent runs arrive as Server-Sent Events: the incremental SSE decoder frames raw byte chunks into typed HermesStreamEvent objects with done/error detection, and pending tool approvals surface as immutable HermesApprovalRequest values the operator must answer. ADR 0006 documents the whole lifecycle — run events drive transcript deltas, tool progress, approvals, and stop controls, with per-session stream ownership and bounded timeouts. This is the heart of what makes Wing feel live.

tour.title: The HermesChannel Facade
tour.description: HermesChannel is the abstract contract for everything the UI can do with a gateway — connection, sessions, profiles, providers, models, messaging, approvals, voice. HermesApiChannel implements it as a ChangeNotifier facade over the HTTP client from Step 5, delegating to eight part files (connection, sessions, profiles, providers, messaging, approvals, voice, errors); with 21 outgoing dependencies it is the widest hub in the graph. Immutable HermesChannelState snapshots expose capability-derived permission getters like canCreateSessions that the UI reads instead of touching raw capabilities.
tour.languageLesson: Dart 'part'/'part of' splits one library across files that share private members — HermesApiChannel stays a single class while its eight concerns live in separate part files.

tour.title: Riverpod Wiring and the Chat Screen
tour.description: hermes_channel_provider.dart is where the abstract channel meets the app: Riverpod providers construct the secure endpoint store, the native HermesApiChannel, the gateway summary loader, and the auto-started connection. ADR 0002 explains the rule — providers are the dependency-injection seam, so tests and E2E entry points override providers rather than reaching for globals. The chat screen consumes it all, stitching nine part files covering connection, layout, lifecycle, and messaging into the app's main surface.
tour.languageLesson: Riverpod providers are lazily-created, override-able singletons: production code reads them via ref.watch, while tests swap implementations with ProviderScope(overrides: [...]) — no service locator needed.

tour.title: Gateway Directory and the Office
tour.description: Wing supports multiple gateways at once. GatewayContact models each saved gateway's identity, availability, and overview snapshot with JSON persistence, and the gateway directory service keeps the contact list fresh, refreshing availability via the API and tracking which gateway is active. The Office screen renders this directory as a 2D card grid of agents with availability labels, skeleton loading, and navigation into each gateway's chat — the 'contacts view' of your agent fleet.

tour.title: Enrollment and the Trust Model
tour.description: Before any of the previous steps can run, a device must be paired: the enrollment screen implements the one-time Android enrollment flow from ADR 0016, exchanging a pairing payload for a stored gateway credential. The threat model document frames why this matters — protected assets, trust boundaries, current controls, and known gaps. Wing's core security stance is that the gateway is trusted after explicit pairing, and everything else fails closed.

tour.title: Device Voice: STT and TTS
tour.description: Voice is deliberately local: ADR 0009 chose on-device speech_to_text for capture (fail closed, no cloud STT) and flutter_tts plus the pinned pocket_speech package for replies. voice_capture_platform.dart resolves the current platform via conditional imports, and the voice input controller owns the whole lifecycle — single capture-and-send plus a continuous hands-free mode that speaks new assistant replies via the TTS service — so the chat widget from Step 8 only renders state.

tour.title: Platform Shells
tour.description: One Dart codebase, several native hosts. The Android manifest declares INTERNET, RECORD_AUDIO, and Bluetooth permissions plus the singleTop MainActivity that receives pairing handoff intents; on Windows, flutter_window.cpp builds the Win32 host window, wires the desktop_host_commands MethodChannel (the other end of Step 2's listener), and adds a native application menu. These shells are thin on purpose — platform code exists only where Flutter cannot reach.
tour.languageLesson: Flutter MethodChannels are the bridge between Dart and native code: both sides agree on a channel name string, then exchange method calls with codec-serialized arguments — Kotlin and C++ hosts implement the same pattern.

tour.title: Testing Strategy
tour.description: Testing leans on the seams from Steps 7-8: fake_hermes_channel.dart — the single highest fan-in node in the graph — simulates sessions, streaming turns, approvals, and voice runs so widget tests drive the full UI without a gateway. main_e2e.dart is a dedicated web entry point exposing a JS hook so Playwright can inject a channel, with flutter_semantics.mjs driving the app through its accessibility DOM. Maestro YAML flows like chat_ux_qa.yaml add on-device Android QA with screenshot capture.

tour.title: CI, Release, and Readiness
tour.description: The platform-smoke workflow is the everyday gate: format, analyze, tests with a 50% coverage floor, a Playwright-driven browser smoke against the built web app, and Linux/Android artifacts. The manually dispatched release workflow validates the alpha tag against pubspec.yaml, reruns all gates, and builds signed APK/AAB packages, while audit_hermes_readiness.sh checks runbooks, receipts, and device prerequisites before a release is declared ready. Together they close the loop from the code you toured back to shippable builds.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use 'on' triggers (push vs workflow_dispatch for manual releases), a job matrix for parallel platform builds, and sequential steps within each job — gating later steps on earlier ones.
